headline: Afghan pacer Shapoor Zadran dies aged 38 after rare immune disorder treatment
summary: Former Afghanistan fast bowler Shapoor Zadran passed away on Tuesday, a day before his 39th birthday. He was reportedly undergoing treatment for a severe immune system disorder in New Delhi.
details: Former Afghanistan fast bowler Shapoor Zadran died on Tuesday, just a day before his 39th birthday. He had been undergoing treatment for a rare and severe immune system disorder at a hospital in New Delhi.

The Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) announced his passing with profound grief. They recognized Zadran as one of the foundational figures of Afghan cricket, whose dedication and passion were vital to the sport's rise in the country.
Zadran, a left-arm pace bowler, made his ODI debut in 2009. He represented Afghanistan in 80 international matches across all formats, including 44 ODIs and 36 T20Is.
He played a crucial role in one of Afghanistan's most significant cricketing achievements: hitting the winning boundary in their first-ever World Cup victory against Scotland in 2015.

headline_marked: 18 injured as [[bombs explode near hotel during Macron's Syria visit]]
headline: 18 injured as bombs explode near hotel during Macron's Syria visit
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron visited Damascus up until Tuesday, where at least two explosions occurred near his hotel, causing widespread panic in the city.
details: At least 18 people, including four police officers, were injured in at least two explosions that occurred near a hotel in Damascus, Syria, on Tuesday, July 7.
The blasts occurred while French President Emmanuel Macron was visiting the city. French authorities stated that Macron was not harmed and did not even hear the explosions during the incident.
At the time of the blasts, Macron was on his way to the residence of Syrian President Ahmed al-Shara to hold a meeting.
The Syrian government reported that the explosions caused widespread panic across various areas of the city.
This visit marks the first time a top European leader has visited Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime.
The incident has raised international concerns regarding the ongoing security risks in the country.
caption:
18 people injured as bombs explode in Damascus during French President Emmanuel Macron's visit.

At least 18 people, including four police officers, were injured in at least two explosions that occurred near a hotel in Damascus, Syria, on Tuesday, July 7.

The blasts occurred while French President Emmanuel Macron was visiting the city. French authorities stated that Macron was not harmed and did not even hear the explosions during the incident.

At the time of the blasts, Macron was on his way to the residence of Syrian President Ahmed al-Shara to hold a meeting.

The Syrian government reported that the explosions caused widespread panic across various areas of the city.

This visit marks the first time a top European leader has visited Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime.

The incident has raised international concerns regarding the ongoing security risks in the country.
